description.narrative:
Sida stödjer konsortiet Somali Resilience Program (SomReP) under en tredje fas för projektet "SomReP 3: Inkluderande försörjningsmöjligheter för utsatta pastorala grupper" med en budget på 79 miljoner SEK under en tvåårigaktivitetssperiod mellan september 2024 och augusti 2026. Projektet bygger på erfarenheter och lärdomar av Sidas stöd till SomReP fas 1 (2013-2016) och fas 2 (2019-2023). Projektet kommer fortsatt rikta sig mot samma geografiska områden i norra Somalia, i de federala medlemsländerna Somaliland och Puntland.
Målet med insatsen är att öka motståndskraften hos kroniskt utsatta människor mot klimatchocker och relaterade risker för att minska humanitära behov i pastorala och agropastorala i Somaliland och Puntland.
Projektet kommer inkludera 145 803 individer i 24 300 hushåll i de två regionerna. Målgruppen inkluderar främst pastoralister och agropastoralister, med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar. Målgruppen omfattar cirka 11 % av personer med funktionshinder.
Projektet fokuserar på fem områden: Adaptiv riskhantering; Chockrepons; Hållbar försörjning och ekonomisk tillväxt; Transparent, ansvarsfull och inkluderande institutionell styrning; samt Adaptiv förvaltning och innovation. Projektet inkluderar Sidas fem utvecklingsperspektiv, inklusive ett resiliens/nexusperspektiv.

Sida support the consortium Somali Resilience Program (SomReP) during a third phase, for the project "SomReP 3: Inclusive livelihoods for vulnerable pastoral groups" with a budget of 79 million SEK during a two year activity period between September 2024 to August 2026. This is based on successful experiences and lessons learnt from the Sida support to SomReP phase 1 (2013-2016) and phase 2 (2019-2023). The project will continue to target the same geographical areas and communities in Northern Somalia, in the federal member states of Somaliland and Puntland.
The principal objective of the contribution is to increase the resilience of chronically vulnerable people to climate-shocks and related risks to reduce humanitarian needs in targeted pastoral, agro-pastoral and peri-urban communities in Somaliland and Puntland.
The project aims to target 145 803 individuals in 24 300 households. The target population mainly include pastoralists and agro-pastoralists, with specific focus on women and youth. The target population includes approximately 11% of people with disability.
The project focuses on five areas: Adaptive risk management; Shock response programme; Sustainable livelihoods & economic growth; Transparent, accountable & inclusive governance; and, Evidence for adaptive management & innovation. The project is in line with Sida's five perspectives and also integrates a resilience/nexus perspective.

The principal objective of the contribution is to increase the resilience of chronically vulnerable people to climate-shocks and related risks to reduce humanitarian needs in targeted pastoral, agro-pastoral and peri-urban communities in Somaliland and Puntland.
The expected outcomes of the contribution are:
Outcome 1 (Adaptive Risk Management): Improved capacity of households to implement effective disaster risk management and positive coping strategies to mitigate the immediate and future effects of exposure to shocks.
Outcome 2 (Shock Response Programme): Improved capacity of individuals, households and communities to adhere to positive development pathways, increase productivity and adapt through climate sensitive approaches, despite exposure to shocks from both rapid and slow-onset hazards.
Outcome 3 (Sustainable Livelihoods & Economic Growth): Improved capacity of pastoralist, agropastoral, and peri-urban households, to engage in strategies for sustainable livelihoods and economic growth to enhance food security and resilience.
Outcome 4 (Transparent, Accountable & Inclusive Governance): Transparent and accountable governance structures at the community, district and national levels established to ensure an enabling policy and regulatory environment for sustainable livelihoods and economic growth to enhance food security and resilience.
Outcome 5 (Evidence for Adaptive Management & Innovation): Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning systems are equipped with a data management platform, which forms the evidence base for informed decision making and strategic programming among relevant stakeholders.
